text: Camp Narache. Camp Narache is a secluded village nestled upon Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It serves as the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe and the proving ground where young tauren begin their training. Sheltered high above the plains, the camp maintains ancient traditions while constantly guarding against encroaching quilboar and lingering centaur threats. Situated at the northern edge of the elevated Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache is the primary settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. The village consists of several large hide lodges and pavilions, including a communal tent for wounded braves, an armory, a bakery tent, and a spirit lounge dedicated to meditation and ancestral communion. At the center of the camp, tribal elders and path trainers stand in a circle at the heart of the camp, where the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind still offers guidance, guiding newly initiated youth as they step into their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother.

Camp Narache is the starting village for young tauren, located atop Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It is the central encampment of the Hawkwind tribe, serving as a sanctuary where fledgling hunters, warriors, druids, and shamans master their crafts before traveling outward to Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff.

Chief Hawkwind guides the tribe's braves and coordinates the defenses of the mesa, alongside the tribe's revered elder, Greatmother Hawkwind. The tribe's trainers and elders gather at the center of the camp to instruct young adventurers.

The encampment is continually harassed by Bristleback quilboar operating out of Brambleblade Ravine to the east. In addition to feral battleboars and striders wandering the surrounding bluffs, the lingering danger of predatory centaur bands keeps the Hawkwind braves on constant alert.

Red Cloud Mesa is naturally bounded by sheer cliffs. The only way down into the greater plains of Mulgore is along a guarded mountain path leading north, watched over by Hawkwind braves to prevent hostile beasts and quilboar from ambushing travelers.

Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-covered vale tucked into the southwestern heights of Dun Morogh. Centered around the hamlet of Anvilmar, it serves as the training ground where young dwarves and gnome refugees first take up arms in service of Ironforge. A single tunnel, Coldridge Pass, connects this secluded hollow to the wider mountain realm. Cradled by sheer mountain cliffs, Coldridge Valley remains largely cut off from the bustling trade routes of Dun Morogh. At its heart sits Anvilmar, a sturdy stone hall and hamlet where veteran dwarven instructors and displaced gnome scholars train fresh recruits in the arts of battle, stealth, and sorcery. Outside the warmth of Anvilmar's hearths, the valley floor is carpeted in thick snow and prowled by boars and hungry winter wolves, providing novices with their first real taste of frontier survival.

The only overland route out of the valley leads through Coldridge Pass, a snowy tunnel cutting northeast through the mountain ridge. Once through the pass, the road heads east directly toward the town of Kharanos and onward to the great gates of Ironforge.

Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radioactive fallout, surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh as refugees. High Tinker Mekkatorque's people were welcomed by King Magni Bronzebeard, leading many exiled gnomish apprentices to train side by side with young dwarves in Anvilmar.

The valley faces two major menaces: the hostile Frostmane trolls, who resent dwarven settlements on their mountain territory, and crude Rockjaw troggs, who have clawed up from the deep earth to choke Coldridge Pass. Local predators like wolves and boars also harass unwary travelers.

Anvilmar is the central fortress-lodge and settlement within Coldridge Valley. It houses class trainers, forge-masters, and local mountaineer officers who coordinate the defense of the valley and prepare newly forged adventurers for the wider world.

Deathknell. Deathknell is a fortified village nestled in a secluded valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the primary awakening grounds for newly freed undead breaking free from the Lich King's grasp to join the Forsaken. Besieged by mindless Scourge remnants, local zealots, and aggressive wildlife, the settlement is a harsh proving ground for those claiming a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. Tucked away behind jagged hills just north of the Silverpine border, Deathknell is where newly awakened undead first open their eyes to their bleak reality. Unlike most settlements in Tirisfal Glades that preserved their human names from the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, Deathknell was explicitly renamed by the undead who claimed it. The town itself is cleaved in two: the Forsaken cling stubbornly to the southern grounds around the old church, while the northern half—including the village forge—remains overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley securely sealed against intruders, allowing local caretakers to induct new arrivals into the Banshee Queen's service.

While most settlements throughout Tirisfal Glades retained their human Lordaeron names, Deathknell is a notable exception. The Forsaken chose the moniker intentionally upon taking root in the valley, marking the site as both the death of their old human existence and the grim bell sounding their rebirth into undeath.

Not every corpse raised in the wake of the Third War broke free with their minds intact. The northern village square and forge are infested by the 'Mindless Ones'—feral zombies, ghouls, and skeletons still driven by the residual, lingering will of the Scourge. Forsaken defenders regularly clear them out to salvage equipment and defend the church.

A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade maintains an encampment in the hills southeast of the village. Fanatically dedicated to destroying all undead indiscriminately, they monitor the pass, ambush newly awakened Forsaken, and exchange scouting intelligence with Scarlet strongholds elsewhere in Lordaeron.

Night Web's Hollow, the gold mine situated in the cliffs northwest of the village, is completely overrun by aggressive spiders. Securing natural resources like gold is critical for the Forsaken war effort, but until the infestation is cleared, the settlement cannot exploit the vein.

Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey is a historic monastery nestled in Northshire Valley within the northern foothills of Elwynn Forest. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a premier training center for new defenders answering the kingdom of Stormwind's call. Centuries ago, clerics from Lordaeron traveled south into the kingdom of Stormwind to spread the worship of the Holy Light, establishing the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery quickly became an anchor of kingdom life, caring for the sick and even tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. During the First War, the abbey suffered repeated assaults by brigands and the Orcish Horde, culminating in its utter destruction. When the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary, refounding its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

The Brotherhood of Northshire is a religious order of clerics, priests, and paladins based out of Northshire Abbey. Originally founded centuries ago by missioning clerics from Lordaeron, it was re-established by Archbishop Alonsus Faol after the First War to train faithful defenders and preserve sacred scripture.

During the First War, the abbey held strategic and spiritual importance for Stormwind. Orcish forces incited human brigands to attack it, and after the half-orc Garona was briefly held captive there, a massive Horde onslaught leveled the holy grounds. It remained ruined throughout the war until the Alliance drove out the orcish clans and rebuilt it.

Stormwind's military is stretched thin protecting distant borders, leaving outlying regions poorly guarded. Opportunistic kobolds have infested the local gold mines, while the Defias Brotherhood exploits the gaps to rob travelers, harass the local vineyards, and raid the abbey's library for arcane tomes and holy relics.

During the First War, an ogre chieftain named Turok stole the sacred Tome of Divinity from Northshire Abbey and retreated into the Deadmines. Sir Anduin Lothar led an expedition into the depths to recover the holy scripture, getting trapped until a royal rescue party saved him and returned the tome to the abbey's care.

Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village is a coastal settlement on the southern shores of Durotar, serving as a sanctuary for the Darkspear trolls. Established by Chieftain Vol'jin after his people were driven from their ancestral home on the Echo Isles, the hamlet honors his fallen father, the witch doctor Sen'jin. Today, it stands as a fragile haven focused on survival, herbalism, and reclaiming what was stolen. When the dark witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin was forced to lead the survivors across the strait to the mainland of Durotar. There, nestled beneath coastal cliffs and looking out over the water, they raised crude huts and established Sen'jin Village. The settlement carries the name of Vol'jin's father, the venerable elder who sacrificed himself during the Third War to save their people from coastal murlocs. Despite their close alliance with Thrall's Horde, the trolls here live under the shadow of exile, staring daily across the shallows at the home they lost.

Shadowglen. Shadowglen is a secluded, twilit vale nestled within the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil. Dominated by the great barrow-tree Aldrassil, it serves as the safe haven where young night elves take their first steps into service before journeying out into the wider world. Tucked away in the northeastern canopy of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Bathed in eternal dusk, the vale centers on Aldrassil, a massive barrow-tree whose hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors for young night elves beginning their training. The only route out of the valley leads south through a narrow mountain pass toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar, making Shadowglen one of the most naturally fortified and peaceful sanctuaries on the World Tree.

Shadowglen is the sheltered starting grove for the night elves, located in the northeastern reaches of Teldrassil. It is a peaceful, secluded haven centered around the grand tree Aldrassil, where novices train under mentors before journeying across the World Tree.

The tree is Aldrassil, a barrow-tree that forms the heart of Shadowglen. Its hollowed interior serves as an administrative lodge and training hub where novice night elves meet class trainers, mentors, and caretakers.

The primary threat comes from the northwest in Shadowthread Cave, a cavern infested with venomous spiders that regularly creep out into the glade. Young defenders are tasked with culling the spiders and calming the restless local wildlife.
Shadowglen is entirely surrounded by ridges except for a single path to the south. Passing through this narrow mountain gap leads southward toward Starbreeze Village and the settlement of Dolanaar.

Valley of Trials. Tucked away behind the rugged red cliffs of southern Durotar, the Valley of Trials serves as the testing ground for new recruits of the Horde. Young orcs and their Darkspear troll allies come here to prove their strength and earn their place among the warriors of Kalimdor. Those who survive the valley's harsh wildlife and hidden threats depart ready to defend their fledgling nation. The Valley of Trials is designed to weed out the weak before they ever set foot in the broader reaches of Durotar. Overseen by chieftains and trainers stationed in the carved cliffside shelter known as The Den, young fighters are thrust into the sun-scorched gulch to hunt scorpids, culled aggressive boars, and enforce discipline among lazy peons harvesting scarce timber. The trial is uncompromising: those who prove their mettle earn the right to venture forth as true soldiers of the Horde, while those who fail are left to bleach beneath the desert sun.

It is the traditional proving ground for recruits of the Horde, primarily young orcs and Darkspear trolls. Within its sheltered canyons, new adventurers complete rigorous tasks to demonstrate their martial skill, survival instinct, and loyalty before being permitted to leave for the rest of Durotar.

The Den is a cave carved into the cliffs roughly in the center of the valley. It houses class trainers, vendors, and overseers like Gornek who direct new recruits, equip them, and monitor their progress during their initial trials.

Cultists belonging to the Burning Blade have established a secret coven in the northern caves. Although trainers use their weak familiars to test recruits, the cult's presence suggests shadowy forces like the Shadow Council are seeking a foothold right on Durotar's doorsteps.

Sarkoth is an unusually large, venomous scorpid residing in the rocky heights of the valley. Due to his aggression and lethality, instructors task promising recruits with hunting him down to test their courage and bring back his mangled claw as proof.

Skyborne. The Skyborne, or shen'dorei, are an offshoot of high elves descended from rebels who fled Eldre'Thalas after opposing Prince Tortheldrin's demonic pacts. Striking a desperate bargain with wind spirits, their ancestors escaped Azeroth to dwell atop the floating Zephras Isle within Skywall. Today, with their elemental benefactors abruptly gone, their floating sanctuary faces internal fractures and physical collapse. Following the Sundering, the Shen'dralar of Eldre'Thalas languished without the Well of Eternity. Prince Tortheldrin devised a dark salvation: summon the demon Immol'thar and siphon its power. Horrified nobles and citizens resisted, fearing another Legion invasion. In response, Tortheldrin executed a bloody purge of dozens of houses. From the surviving shadows rose a resistance spearheaded by a masked figure known only as the Shal'nan ('the Veiled One'). When a desperate rebel raid on Tortheldrin's ritual sanctum descended into catastrophic chaotic magic, the Shal'nan rallied the survivors and fled west to the port of Eldre'narr, taking to the seas pursued by the Prince's fleet.

The Skyborne, or shen'dorei ('the hidden people'), are high elves descended from ancient night elves who rebelled against Prince Tortheldrin in Eldre'Thalas. To escape his vengeful fleet, they struck a pact with wind spirits, who relocated their island, Zephras Isle, into the Elemental Plane of Air.

Millennia in the Elemental Plane of Air have subtly reshaped their biology. A recent phenomenon known as the Sky-Touched Blessing causes an increasing proportion of children—now roughly three out of ten—to be born with blue skin. Scholars predict their ancestral night elf traits will soon be entirely supplanted.

The Shal'nan, or 'the Veiled One', was the masked leader who spearheaded the resistance against Prince Tortheldrin's demon summoning in Eldre'Thalas. After leading the survivors to safety in Skywall, he abdicated to establish a democratic council, serving his people until mysteriously vanishing centuries ago alongside their elemental benefactors.

Zephras Isle is held aloft within Skywall by magical pylons attuned to elemental power. When the wind spirits who maintained them abruptly disappeared centuries ago, the anchoring pylons began to fail. Portions of the landmass have broken off into the void, stranding survivors and driving displaced elves to banditry.

They are the two primary cultural factions of the Skyborne. The High Order descends from Highborne magisters and seeks to rebuild their crumbling society through disciplined arcane mastery. The Windshapers trace their roots to ordinary night elf citizens and revere the elemental and spiritual customs cultivated during their time in Skywall.

The Al'Aketh are a desperate cult of Skyborne who worship Al'Akir the Windlord. While their ancestors' elemental benefactors feared and avoided speaking of Al'Akir, the collapse of Zephras Isle led homeless and disenfranchised refugees to turn to the elemental lord for salvation and power.

Ashenvale. Ashenvale is the ancient, rain-drenched ancestral forest of the night elves, held sacred under the protection of the Sentinels and the demigod Cenarius. Bordering the Barrens to the south and Darkshore to the north, it has erupted into a bitter war zone as the Horde harvests timber to build its young nation. Ancient trees and tranquil moonwells share canopy with demonic holdouts, hostile beastmen, and clash points along the contested frontier. Stretching beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has stood for millennia under the stewardship of the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius. Immense trees knit together into a dense canopy that turns daily rain into a gentle mist and casts the forest floor in eternal twilight. Ancient ruins of elven civilization poke through the moss, guarded by walking ancients and dryads. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here, preferring to hunt lightly and preserve the wild domain in pristine balance.

The Barrens. The Barrens is an expansive, sun-baked savanna that serves as the beating geographical and logistical heart of the Horde in central Kalimdor. Once a verdant forest prior to the Great Sundering, it is now an arid plain of red dust, hardy scrub, and wandering wildlife. Centered around the strategic hub of the Crossroads, the land remains locked in constant struggle against quilboar tribes, centaur raiders, and creeping corruption. For countless generations, nomadic tauren hunted kodo and zhevra across these plains while waging a defensive, cyclical war against marauding Kolkar centaur. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor during the Third War, he aided Cairne Bloodhoof in repelling the centaur and traversing the savanna into Mulgore. Today, the Barrens connects Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale. Outposts like the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo secure trade along the Gold Road, while orcish homesteads brave the arid climate to forge a lasting home.

Blackfathom Deeps. Blackfathom Deeps is a flooded subterranean temple complex situated along the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Once a shrine dedicated to the night elven moon goddess Elune, the sunken sanctuary has been overtaken by the Twilight's Hammer cult, treacherous naga, and satyrs. They gather in its dark waters to venerate and nurture Aku'mai, a primordial pet and herald of the Old Gods. Long before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this complex was known as Lathar'Lazal, a splendid temple dedicated to Elune. Highborne masons raised gem-encrusted bridges while Queen Azshara commanded the surrounding waters, partitionining salt seas and mountain streams around a sacred moonwell. When the Sundering tore the world apart ten thousand years ago, the temple sank into the coastal depths of the Veiled Sea. For millenia, it sat undisturbed beneath the waves—until foul whispers began seeping upward from the subterranean dark.

Darkshore. Darkshore is a cold, mist-shrouded strip of coast lining northwestern Kalimdor, dotted with ancient Kaldorei ruins and troubled wildlife. Anchored by the Alliance harbor town of Auberdine, it serves as the primary continental gateway for travelers arriving from Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond the patrolled road, demonic cults, encroaching naga, and a creeping corruption from the highlands threaten the region's delicate balance. Stretching beneath the western shadows of Mount Hyjal and Felwood, Darkshore is characterized by pine groves, sea fog, and rocky beaches beaten by cold waves. Millennia ago, this coast was home to the flourishing Kaldorei twin cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. Shattered during the Great Sundering, their skeletal pillars and marble arches now lie half-drowned in the surf or overgrown with roots, haunted by restless Highborne spirits and overrun by scavenger murlocs and invasive naga.

Darnassus. Darnassus is the serene, open-air capital city of the night elves, built amidst the branches of the newly planted World Tree, Teldrassil. Governed by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind alongside the druids of the Cenarion Enclave, it serves as a tranquil sanctuary for an ancient people adapting to mortality. Sheltered across vast terraces surrounding a crystalline lake, it stands as the heart of night elf society and their bridge to the Alliance. Unlike the dense masonry of Stormwind or the carved stone tunnels of Ironforge, Darnassus is broad, quiet, and intimately open to the wilderness. Formed upon the upper canopy of Teldrassil off northern Kalimdor's coast, the capital's graceful wooden structures and winding pathways encircle a tranquil central lake. Elegant bridges connect terraces dedicated to tradesmen, craftsmen, sentinels, and druids, creating an atmosphere that balances civic governance with profound reverence for nature.

Because Teldrassil is an island isolated off Kalimdor's northwest coast, travelers must reach Rut'theran Village at the foot of the tree by boat or flight. From the village docks, a glowing magical transport tentacle takes travelers directly up into the city boughs.

High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules Darnassus and the kaldorei from the grand Temple of the Moon. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave, acting as the de facto druidic authority while Malfurion Stormrage remains lost in the Emerald Dream.

Darnassus was founded shortly after the Third War. When the night elves sacrificed their immortality to defeat Archimonde at Mount Hyjal, Fandral Staghelm pushed to grow the new World Tree, Teldrassil, to reclaim their former state. Darnassus was carved into the boughs as their new refuge.

Malfurion Stormrage is missing, his spirit trapped within the Emerald Dream. In his absence, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm governs the druids of Teldrassil, while Tyrande Whisperwind continually seeks a way to awaken and recover her beloved mate.

The city is divided into specialized terraces. The Craftsmen's Terrace hosts gathering and tailoring disciplines along with an inn, while the Tradesmen's Terrace houses trade stalls and the Auction House. Blacksmithing and martial trainers reside on the Warrior's Terrace, and the city bank rests upon the central island of the Temple Gardens.

After the devastation of the Third War, the night elves faced mounting pressure from the Horde, particularly orcish logging expeditions into Ashenvale. Recognizing the need for allies against these incursions and other rising threats across Kalimdor, Darnassus opened diplomatic ties and joined the Grand Alliance.

The Deadmines. Deep beneath the dusty farm town of Moonbrook lies the Deadmines, an enormous subterranean complex that once supplied a third of Stormwind's gold reserves. Abandoned during the First War and long considered haunted, these labyrinthine tunnels have secretly been overtaken by the Defias Brotherhood as their ultimate staging ground. Here, Edwin VanCleef and his conscripted goblin engineers labor away from the eyes of the realm to build an engine of vengeance against the kingdom. Before the First War, the Deadmines were celebrated as the greatest gold-producing center in human lands, financing the prosperity of Stormwind. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to the dark. During those turbulent years, legendary figures walked these depths: Sir Anduin Lothar was imprisoned by subterranean ogres for twenty months while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity, and Warchief Blackhand's rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages alongside the ogre Turok before both met their ends. Believed to be cursed and populated only by shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.

Dun Morogh. Dun Morogh is a snow-swept mountain highland situated at the heart of Khaz Modan. It serves as the ancestral starting ground and shared homeland for the dwarves of Ironforge and the displaced gnomes of Gnomeregan. Though guarded by towering peaks and fortified passes, the snowy realm faces rising internal threats from troggs, Frostmane trolls, and irradiated leper gnomes. Dun Morogh occupies the highest peaks in the Eastern Kingdoms, an alpine expanse ringed by jagged summits that shield it from Searing Gorge to the south and the Wetlands to the north. These snowy mountains feed the rivers flowing across Khaz Modan and provide near-limitless veins of copper and iron. Access is heavily restricted to mountain tunnels like North Gate Pass and South Gate Pass, watched closely by dwarven Mountaineers. At the heart of the region sits Ironforge, an ancient subterranean wonder and the capital of King Magni Bronzebeard's realm, linked straight to Stormwind by the marvel of the Deeprun Tram.
Both dwarves and gnomes begin their journeys here in Coldridge Valley, a sheltered basin in southwestern Dun Morogh, before venturing out through Coldridge Pass into Kharanos and the wider zone.

During the Third War, a subterranean race called troggs swarmed Gnomeregan. In an attempt to purge the invaders, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque released radioactive gas into the lower levels. The plan failed catastrophically, killing thousands and irradiating many gnomes into crazed leper gnomes, forcing the healthy survivors to flee to Ironforge.

Dun Morogh is walled in by high mountain ridges. To travel eastward into Loch Modan on foot, take the roads leading to North Gate Pass or South Gate Pass in the northeastern mountains. You can also travel directly to Stormwind City via the Deeprun Tram inside Ironforge.

The only functional Alliance flight master in the zone is located inside the Great Forge of Ironforge, connecting travelers to locations across Khaz Modan, Stormwind, and the northern Alliance outposts.

The Frostmane are a tribe of ice trolls who ruled Dun Morogh long before the dwarves emerged from Uldaman. Though defeated and driven into the crags generations ago, they remain bitter enemies of Ironforge, routinely raiding dwarven farms and roads from retreats like Frostmane Hold.

Kharanos is the primary dwarven settlement in central Dun Morogh. It houses the Thunderbrew Distillery, trainers, and supplies, serving as the central operational hub for young adventurers and Mountaineers tackling local troll and wildlife problems.

Durotar. Durotar is the arid, red-rock homeland founded by Warchief Thrall following the Third War, named in honor of his father, Durotan. Bounded by the Southfury River and the Great Sea, it serves as the heartland of the New Horde and the proving ground for young orcs and Darkspear trolls. Within its harsh canyons lie fortified settlements like Razor Hill, the sprawling warrior city of Orgrimmar, and entrenched hostile holdouts ranging from quilboar tribes to stranded Alliance troops. When Thrall led his people across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he deliberately sought an untamed frontier where the orcs could carve out an honest existence through labor and grit rather than conquest. Durotar's cracked red soil, baked gullies, and towering red-rock spires remind the orcs deeply of Draenor before its destruction. While the climate is unforgiving, offering little arable land and sparse water, the Horde embraced the landscape's natural defense and austere majesty. Bordered to the west across the Southfury River by the open Barrens and to the north by the ruined wilderness of Azshara, Durotar stands as living proof that the orcs have forged their own destiny.

Thrall chose this unforgiving territory intentionally. The red earth and rugged mesas reminded the orcs of their ancestral world of Draenor, while its harsh conditions served as penance and a forge for discipline. Thrall believed his people needed to earn their survival through honest hardship rather than claiming fertile lands by conquest, ensuring they would not slide back into bloodthirsty complacency.

The land was named in honor of Durotan, Thrall's late father and the former chieftain of the Frostwolf clan. Durotan had opposed the demonic corruption of the orcish clans and was murdered on the orders of the warlock Gul'dan.

The soldiers at Tiragarde Keep are surviving Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict, left over from Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion fleet. Even after Proudmoore was slain, these troops refused to surrender or withdraw, maintaining an entrenched hostile outpost right on Durotar's southern coast.

The Darkspear trolls originally established their Kalimdor home on the Echo Isles. However, a powerful witch doctor named Zalazane succumbed to madness and turned his dark magic against his brethren, enslaving their minds. The survivors fled to the mainland to establish Sen'jin Village, from which they launch raids to break his hold.

The Burning Blade is a subversive demonic cult loyal to the Shadow Council and the Burning Legion. Operatives lurk in secluded spots like Skull Rock and the Burning Blade Coven, attempting to undermine Thrall's leadership and tempt impressionable orcs back into demonic servitude.

A bridge over the Southfury River leads west into the Barrens, while a path through northern Orgrimmar crosses into Azshara. Outside Orgrimmar, twin zeppelin towers provide transcontinental air travel directly to Tirisfal Glades and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

Duskwood. Once a sunlit expanse of southern Elwynn known as Brightwood, Duskwood is now a cursed woodland trapped beneath an unnatural, perpetual gloom. Abandoned by the authorities in Stormwind, its besieged human inhabitants cling to survival in Darkshire under the watchful protection of the local Night Watch militia. Across its darkened groves and haunted barrows roam flesh-eating ghouls, gigantic venomous spiders, raiding ogres, and savage, mysterious worgen. Before the darkness descended, this province was known as Brightwood, a rich agricultural tract of the Kingdom of Stormwind boasting prosperous settlements like Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill. The region's tragedy began when Guardian Medivh fell at Karazhan during the First War, unleashing waves of corrupted fel magic that twisted the serene woodland into a gnarled, shadowy morass. Spiders mutated into terrifying predatory beasts, while fleeing wolves spilled north into Elwynn Forest. Over time, Grand Hamlet was rechristened Darkshire, its terrified townsfolk left largely to fend for themselves as the realm's royal garrison withdrew to defend the capital.

Elwynn Forest. Elwynn Forest is the verdant heartland of the Kingdom of Stormwind, providing the capital with essential timber, gold, fish, and crops. Sheltered beneath stately hardwoods, it serves as the proving ground for new human recruits stepping forth from Northshire Abbey. Yet beneath its idyllic pastoral canopy, the woods are sorely beleaguered by encroaching vermin, displaced wildlife, and widespread brigandage. Stretching south from the gates of Stormwind down to the Nazferiti River, Elwynn is a fertile region blessed with abundant rainfall and dense hardwood forests. Communities like Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp provide crucial grain, livestock, lumber, and raw copper to sustain the grand capital. The region is also celebrated for breeding sturdy Evendale horses, favored by travelers and knights across the kingdom.

Stormwind's armed forces are severely overstretched. The kingdom expanded heavy military deployments southward into Stranglethorn Vale, running up deep debts and draining local manpower. As a result, outposts like Westbrook Garrison and Goldshire rely on small skeleton crews and volunteer recruits to fight off bandits, gnolls, and murlocs.

With guards in short supply, opportunistic kobolds swarmed into Fargodeep Mine, Jasperlode Mine, and Echo Ridge Mine in search of precious gold and minerals. They drove out the human prospectors and miners, aggressively defending their subterranean claims with candles, crude picks, and scavenged tools.

They are members of the Defias Brotherhood, led by Edwin VanCleef. Many were originally artisans of the Stonemasons Guild who rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War. When the nobility refused to pay them their promised wages, riots broke out, leading to their banishment and descent into organized brigandage.

Crossing the bridge over the Nazferiti River takes you into Duskwood, historically known as Brightwood. That once-peaceful territory has fallen into unnatural darkness and is now infested with undead, monstrous spiders, and ravenous beasts.

The Stonefields and the Maclures are neighboring farming families in southern Elwynn who have maintained a bitter, longstanding grudge against each other. Despite their endless bickering and accusations, two of their younger kin—Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield—have secretly fallen in love, complicating the rivalry even further.

The Tower of Azora is an arcane spire located along the road between Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp. It houses secluded mages, including Theocritus, who observe the region's leylines and conduct magical research outside the direct oversight of Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum.

Gnomeregan. Carved into the snowy foothills of Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan was once the subterranean capital and greatest technological wonder of the gnomish race. Today it lies ruined and quarantined, poisoned by radioactive fallout following a desperate defense against an underground trogg invasion. Its surviving people now dwell as refugees in nearby Ironforge, while the irradiated halls remain overrun by mutated troggs, deranged leper gnomes, and rogue mechanical sentries. Long before its tragic fall, Gnomeregan stood as a testament to the heights of gnomish brilliance, ambition, and industry. Constructed with the assistance of the nearby dwarves of Ironforge, the sprawling mechanical complex was powered by giant grinding engines, whirring gears, and an intricate ventilation network that required fifteen technicians working around the clock just to maintain fresh air. It was a thriving center of invention, competitive craft, and politics centered on Tinkers' Court, serving as the proud capital from which gnomes contributed invaluable siege engines, flying machines, and armaments to the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War.

Hall of Thanes. Deep beneath the bustling city of Ironforge lies the Hall of Thanes, an ancient subterranean complex steeped in dwarven history. Intended for early Alliance adventurers, this secluded dungeon holds relics of the mountain kingdom's past that have fallen into peril. Gaining entry requires unearthing forgotten routes through the mountain itself. While Ironforge hums with the ringing of hammers in the Great Forge, forgotten halls delve far deeper beneath the stone. The Hall of Thanes represents one of these venerable subterranean reaches. Long tied to ancestral dwarven bloodlines and relics of stonecraft, it now requires intrepid Alliance champions to venture into its shadowed vaults to secure the depths.

Hillsbrad Foothills. Hillsbrad Foothills is a green, fertile region that represents the last pastoral bastion of the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. Despite having largely escaped the Scourge's plague, the land is torn apart by brutal open war between the humans of Southshore and the Forsaken entrenched at Tarren Mill. It serves as a violent crossroads where the armies of the Alliance and the Horde clash without mercy. While northern Lordaeron rots under the blight of the Scourge, Hillsbrad remains strikingly green. Its rolling pastures, pine groves, and working farmsteads offer travelers a rare glimpse of what the kingdom looked like before the Third War. Yet that tranquil appearance is deceptive. The peaceful fields and rural roads are constantly swept by armed patrols, rogue mercenaries, and scavenger beasts. What should be Lordaeron's breadbasket has instead become its most contested borderland.

Ironforge. Carved into the heart of Ironforge Mountain in snowy Dun Morogh, Ironforge is the ancestral capital of the Bronzebeard dwarves and an unassailable bastion of the Alliance. Centered on the molten heat of the Great Forge, this sprawling underground city serves as a bustling hub of commerce, industry, and ancient dwarven lore. Under the steadfast rule of King Magni Bronzebeard, it now also shelters the displaced gnomes of nearby Gnomeregan. Ironforge was founded twenty-five hundred years ago when the first generation of dwarves awakened in Uldaman and journeyed west into Dun Morogh's jagged peaks. Delving into the tallest mountain, they built a massive shrine to their titan progenitor Khaz'goroth alongside the colossal Great Forge. Ever since, the city has expanded in concentric rings around that fiery hearth. Unlike surface capitals, Ironforge is entirely enclosed beneath stone ceilings, warmed by roaring hearths and subterranean rivers of molten magma. Its fortified gates and cavernous depths have proven near-impregnable throughout centuries of war.

King Magni Bronzebeard rules Ironforge and the kingdom of Khaz Modan from the High Seat. A skilled warrior and master blacksmith, he has governed his people through the Second and Third Wars and remains a deeply loyal pillar of the Alliance.

When the nearby gnomish capital of Gnomeregan fell to a sudden trogg invasion and a disastrous radiation accident, the surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh. King Magni welcomed them into Ironforge, granting them an entire quarter of the city now known as Tinker Town.

The Great Forge is the fiery industrial heart of the city, fed by underground waterfalls of molten magma. It surrounds the Great Anvil, where dwarven weaponsmiths craft legendary arms and armor. King Magni himself forged the famed holy blade Ashbringer upon this anvil.

Ironforge is connected directly to Stormwind City by the Deeprun Tram, an extraordinary subterranean railway built by gnomish engineering that cuts straight through the mountain bedrock of the Eastern Kingdoms.

Ironforge has never fallen to an outside invader. Kilrogg Deadeye's Bleeding Hollow clan laid siege to it for months during the Second War, and the Dark Irons fought into the city during the War of the Three Hammers, but the gates and defenders held.

After the War of the Three Hammers, the defeated Wildhammer clan relocated north into the Wetlands and the Hinterlands, while the hostile Dark Iron clan settled within the Redridge and Blackrock regions under the thrall of the Firelord.

Loch Modan. Loch Modan is a temperate mountain valley east of Dun Morogh, renowned for its massive alpine lake held in place by the monumental Stonewrought Dam. Centered around the dwarven town of Thelsamar, the region struggles under encroaching trogg infestations, kobolds in the mines, and aggressive ogres in the northeast highlands. Situated in eastern Khaz Modan, Loch Modan presents a stark, pleasant contrast to the frozen snowfields of Dun Morogh. Rugged mountain peaks enclose a temperate valley of pine and birch, cradling the Loch itself. This massive body of fresh water is held in place by the Stonewrought Dam, an architectural triumph that towers along the northern rim. The peaceful settlement of Thelsamar serves as the civic heart of the territory, housing traveling mountaineers, hunters, and miners who ply the productive veins of copper and tin scattered throughout the hills.

Mulgore. Mulgore is the ancestral homeland of the tauren, a lush, sheltered valley of emerald grasslands, towering plateaus, and rolling plains nestled beneath the Stonetalon Mountains. Surrounded by high natural mountain walls, the realm was secured after Cairne Bloodhoof allied with Thrall's Horde to drive out the marauding centaur. Today, it serves as the spiritual and territorial heartland of the united tauren tribes, overseen from the great mesa city of Thunder Bluff. For generations, the tauren lived as nomads, perpetually hunted and displaced across the central plains by aggressive centaur warbands. Their fortune shifted when High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof encountered Thrall and his displaced orcs. Recognizing shared ideals of honor, shamanism, and strength, the tauren forged an alliance with the nascent Horde. With orcish assistance, Cairne broke the centaur's grip on the region and led his people into Mulgore. Here, they built permanent settlements for the first time in centuries, crowning the highest northern mesas with their capital, Thunder Bluff.

The tauren were historically a nomadic people who traveled Kalimdor while pursued by centaur marauders. After joining forces with Thrall's Horde, Cairne Bloodhoof gained the military strength needed to drive off the centaur and reclaim the ancestral valley of Mulgore. They constructed permanent settlements, including Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff, to establish a unified homeland where all tauren tribes could thrive in peace.

Mulgore is completely ringed by impassable mountain walls except for a single southeastern pass. Following the main dirt highway east past Bloodhoof Village and Morin Cloudstalker's post leads through this mountain corridor directly into the arid plains of the Barrens.

The Venture Company is an unscrupulous goblin-run commercial cartel seeking Kalimdor's natural riches. In Mulgore, they run a mining operation in the eastern mountains and have occupied the vital water wells—such as Thunderhorn, Wildmane, and Winterhoof—desecrating the land and threatening the regional water supply.

Dwarves from the Bael Modan expedition have established the Bael'dun Digsite in Mulgore's northern foothills. Driven by the Explorers' League to unearth relics of their Titan creators, they excavate tauren land without permission, ignoring tauren protests that such operations scar the Earthmother.

The Rites of the Earthmother are a sacred series of trials that every young tauren undertakes upon reaching adulthood. These tasks test hunting, tracking, vision communion, and knowledge of the natural balance, proving the young initiate's devotion to the land and the ancestral traditions of their people.

High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof governs all tauren lands from the capital city of Thunder Bluff atop the northern mesas. His son, Baine Bloodhoof, governs Bloodhoof Village and manages the daily concerns of the lower plains under Cairne's wisdom.

Orgrimmar. Orgrimmar is the fortress capital of the orcs and the beating heart of Thrall's New Horde. Carved directly into the towering red-rock canyons of northern Durotar, the fortified city stands as a monument to orcish perseverance and an unyielding sanctuary for trolls, tauren, and Forsaken allies alike. Following the Third War, Warchief Thrall led the orcs to the arid coasts of Kalimdor to build a homeland free from demonic corruption and human bondage. Naming the harsh region Durotar after his father, Thrall established Orgrimmar in memory of his fallen mentor, Orgrim Doomhammer. Raising the city required blood and sweat; aided by the tauren, the Darkspear trolls, goblin engineers, and the Champion Rexxar, the Horde drove back encroaching centaur, harpies, and ferocious thunder lizards to secure the canyon stronghold.

Warchief Thrall rules the city from his seat in Grommash Hold. He leads the New Horde with a focus on honor, survival, and shamanistic heritage, supported closely by Darkspear chieftain Vol'jin and veteran commander Varok Saurfang.

Thrall named the city in honor of Orgrim Doomhammer, the legendary former Warchief who broke the shadow council's hold on the Old Horde and passed his warplate and the Doomhammer to Thrall before dying in battle.

While founded by orcs, the city is a haven for the Darkspear troll tribe—who occupy the Valley of Spirits—and hosts visiting tauren ambassadors in the Valley of Wisdom. An emissary contingent of Forsaken has also established a presence following their recent entry into the Horde.

The Cleft of Shadow is a dim, cavernous fissure tucked beneath the canyon bluffs off The Drag. It houses the city's rogue and warlock guilds, keeping their illicit trade and dangerous demonic invocations secluded from the civilian districts.

Directly below the Cleft of Shadow lies Ragefire Chasm, a treacherous network of subterranean volcanic fissures infested with troggs, searing elementals, and treacherous warlocks seeking to undermine Thrall's rule from the depths.

Goblin-engineered zeppelins dock atop towers outside the main gate, providing regular flights across the Great Sea to Tirisfal Glades near Undercity and south to Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

Ragefire Chasm. Ragefire Chasm is a network of winding volcanic tunnels situated directly beneath the orcish capital of Orgrimmar. Entered through the dark hollows of the Cleft of Shadow, the chasm is overrun by savage troggs and a demonic sect of cultists known as the Searing Blade. Left unchecked, the dark powers and subterranean swarms festering below threaten the very foundation of the young Horde nation. Beneath the dust and red rocks of Orgrimmar lies a blistering maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. While orcish builders forged their new home above, aggressive Ragefire troggs began erupting from deep below the surface. Magatha Grimtotem sought to open diplomatic channels with the brutes on behalf of Thunder Bluff, but her envoy Maur Grimtotem was slaughtered, proving the troggs will yield only to force.

Razorfen Kraul. Tucked away in the far south of the Barrens, Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of Kalimdor's quilboar. These ferocious tribes revere the dense labyrinth of giant brambles as the sacred resting place of their progenitor, the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Today, the Kraul has grown aggressively hostile under the tyranny of the quilboar matriarch Charlga Razorflank, whose dark dealings threaten the entire region. Ten thousand years ago during the apocalyptic War of the Ancients, the colossal wild god Agamaggan threw himself into the fight against the Burning Legion. The great boar was eventually slain in battle, yet his sacrifice preserved life on Azeroth. Legends tell that wherever his blood seeped into the earth, massive thorn-covered vines erupted, forming thick, defensive labyrinths across the southern plains. The quilboar, venerating Agamaggan as their divine ancestor, claimed these colossal thickets as their holy lands, establishing the greatest of them as the Razorfen.

Redridge Mountains. East of Elwynn Forest, the Redridge Mountains feature rushing rivers, wooded slopes, and the serene expanse of Lake Everstill. Despite its scenic heights, the region is besieged by hostile Shadowhide gnolls and the encroaching Blackrock orcs of the Dark Horde. With the kingdom's military tied up by internal strife in Stormwind, the lakeside town of Lakeshire must rely on wandering mercenaries to hold the line. The Redridge range was once among the most peaceful corners of the kingdom, supplying Stormwind with timber, freshwater fish, and crops. Today, that quiet life has eroded. The lakeside township of Lakeshire sits perpetually fortified against aggressive incursions. To the east, Stonewatch Keep—once a proud bastion of the kingdom—has fallen under the control of renegade Blackrock orcs and gnolls, cutting off roads and threatening to overrun the eastern valleys entirely.

Ruins of Lordaeron. Perched directly above the subterranean Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollow remains of humanity's once-mighty northern kingdom. Fallen to the Scourge and Prince Arthas during the Third War, the surface streets and cracked plazas now crawl with wandering monstrosities, vengeful specters, and vile experimenters. Both the Alliance and the Horde dispatch ventures into this blighted citadel to reclaim relics of the fallen past or purge the horrors lurking above the Forsaken capital. Capital City was once the crown jewel of the Eastern Kingdoms, the seat of King Terenas Menethil II and the beating heart of human civilization. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he slew his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the citizenry. Today, while the Forsaken dwell in the catacombs of the Undercity below, the surface ruins remain a forsaken twilight zone. Broken archways and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts like Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past.

Scarlet Monastery. Perched in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery was once a peaceful sanctuary and center of learning for the Church of the Holy Light. Following the fall of Lordaeron, it was seized and heavily fortified by the Scarlet Crusade as their primary forward base in the west. Now, it stands as a sprawling stronghold divided into four wings, where fanatical zealots train, torture captives, and wage an uncompromising war against all outsiders. Before the Third War, the monastery served as a proud seat of Lordaeron's priesthood and a seminary for fledgling paladins of the Silver Hand, once cherished by Archbishop Alonsus Faol himself. Following the Scourge's devastation, surviving crusaders purged the halls of lingering undead and spiders, transforming the tranquil archives and courtyards into a fortified garrison. Driven by paranoia and grief, the Scarlet Crusade came to view all outsiders—living or undead, human or otherwise—as carriers of the plague who must be cleansed with fire.

Shadowfang Keep. Perched on the rugged bluffs above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep is the gloomy stronghold of the rogue Kirin Tor wizard, Archmage Arugal. Once the ancestral estate of Baron Silverlaine, the bastion now teems with feral worgen beasts and the tormented phantoms of its slaughtered defenders. For adventurers traversing southern Silverpine, the keep represents the dark epicenter of the beastly scourge consuming the region. Before it was shrouded in nightmare, Shadowfang was known as Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat loyal to Gilnean lords and garrisoned by the pious Commander Springvale. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied Kirin Tor leadership and delved into the research of the wizard Ur, summoning extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The summoned beasts savaged the undead, but rapidly slipped beyond all mortal control, breaking into southern Silverpine and storming the bastion. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls alongside the feral monsters that overran their home.

Silverpine Forest. Silverpine Forest is an eerie, mist-laden woodland stretching along Lordaeron's western coast between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Haunted by the lingering scars of the Scourge plague, it serves as the contested southern frontier of the Forsaken. Travelers here face feral worgen roaming the shadows, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves. Once celebrated as a lush wonder of Lordaeron through which noble travelers journeyed to Capital City, Silverpine Forest has withered under the touch of the Third War. Ghostly fogs weave between dying, silver-barked pines, and ruined farmsteads sit abandoned to the wilderness. To the north lies Tirisfal Glades, while the eastern shore borders Lordamere Lake. To the south stands the imposing and shut Greymane Wall, sealing off the isolationist kingdom of Gilneas from the surrounding chaos. The Forsaken maintain their central outpost at the Sepulcher, striving to secure the woods from enemies on all sides.

The Stockade. The Stockade is Stormwind's high-security prison complex, tucked beneath the city's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built to hold the kingdom's most dangerous cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, the facility has recently collapsed into violent anarchy. Warden Thelwater has been forced back to the threshold, desperately recruiting capable adventurers to crush the riot from within before it spills out into the capital. Beneath the tranquil canals of Stormwind, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched out to fight on distant fronts, the understaffed prison leaned on inexperienced youth—including fourteen-year-old recruits—to maintain order. It did not hold. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tearing their wool blankets into gang scarves and cutting down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely maintained control of the entryway, leaving the cells, hallways, and holding blocks in the ruthless hands of the convicts.

Stonetalon Mountains. The Stonetalon Mountains are a rugged, wind-carved chain of craggy peaks bordering Ashenvale, the Barrens, and Desolace. Revered by both the night elves and the tauren as a sacred sanctuary, the region's sacred heights stand in sharp contrast to the smoke and machinery choking its lower canyons. Today, the mountains are torn by deforestation, volatile elemental devastation, and simmering border hostilities. Rising sharply out of central Kalimdor, the Stonetalon range catches the moisture drifting from the western seas, giving birth to sudden downpours and treacherous, rain-slick sandstone trails. The dominant feature of the lower valleys is the incessant scouring gale known as the Ill Winds, capable of blinding travelers with grit or throwing the careless straight off sheer cliffsides. Higher up, evergreen forests mantle the ridges surrounding Stonetalon Peak, where the night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades, watching over the sacred roosts of wyverns and hippogryphs that nest along Mirkfallon Lake.

Stormwind City. Stormwind City is the bustling capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the premier human bastion in the world following the fall of Lordaeron. Rebuilt from ashes by the Stonemasons Guild after its destruction in the First War, its magnificent white stone districts now house the heart of the Grand Alliance. Beneath its majestic canals and cathedrals, however, the city grapples with the sudden disappearance of King Varian Wrynn and brewing political intrigue. Founded over a millennium ago by the descendants of the Arathi, Stormwind stood for generations as a flourishing, self-sufficient realm. That golden era ended when the Orcish Horde poured through the Dark Portal, laying waste to the southern continent and razing the capital to the ground in the First War. Survivors led by Sir Anduin Lothar fled north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. Following the Horde's defeat in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance funded a complete reconstruction. The Stonemasons Guild painstakingly rebuilt the capital into New Stormwind—a gleaming citadel of polished white stone and canal-laced boroughs.

Ten-year-old Prince Anduin Wrynn holds the crown, but actual governance is handled by Highlord Bolvar Fordragon, who acts as Regent of Stormwind and supreme commander of its military. Bolvar relies heavily on the counsel of royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor while King Varian Wrynn remains missing.

King Varian vanished under suspicious circumstances while traveling by ship to a diplomatic summit in Theramore. His disappearance was kept quiet to maintain stability, though rumors run rampant through the streets and countryside.

The original city was burned to the ground by the Orcish Horde during the First War. After the Second War, the Stonemasons Guild, led by master craftsman Edwin VanCleef, painstakingly rebuilt the capital out of gleaming white stone with financial backing from the Alliance of Lordaeron.

The House of Nobles amassed heavy debts expanding Stormwind's military and refused to pay the Stonemasons Guild their promised wages. When Edwin VanCleef demanded restitution, the nobles disbanded the guild. The workers rioted, Queen Tiffin Wrynn was killed by a thrown rock, and the exiled stonemasons formed the Defias Brotherhood.

The statues honor the Sons of Lothar: General Turalyon, Ranger Captain Alleria Windrunner, Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, and Danath Trollbane. They were raised to commemorate the heroes who ventured through the Dark Portal to draenor to seal the rift and protect Azeroth.

Stormwind is connected to Ironforge by the Deeprun Tram, a subterranean railway built by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to enable swift trade and rapid military reinforcement between both capitals.

The royal court, heavily advised by Lady Katrana Prestor, insists the city cannot spare troops from its own walls and immediate borders. With the kingdom's finances stressed and political infighting paralyzing the House of Nobles, regional towns have been abandoned to rely on local militias.

Teldrassil. Teldrassil, meaning 'Crown of the Earth', is a gargantuan new World Tree raised off Kalimdor's northwest coast. Grown by the druids in the wake of the Third War, its colossal boughs support an entire twilit wilderness and the night elf capital of Darnassus. Yet beneath its tranquil, moonlit canopy, a creeping corruption has begun to stir. Teldrassil is not merely a tree; it is an elevated ecosystem standing tall amidst the waters of the Veiled Sea. Its gargantuan limbs support rolling hills, flowing rivers fed by morning dew, misty lakes, and dense ancient glades. At its western edge sits Darnassus, the grand capital of the kaldorei. At the base of its monumental trunk lies Rut'theran Village, connected to the crown above by a mystical gateway and serving as the island's primary harbor.

After Nordrassil was devastated at the end of the Third War, the night elves lost their immortality. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm pushed the Circle of Ancients and Cenarion druids to plant a new World Tree in the sea, aiming to restore what their people had lost.

Nordrassil originally granted immortality because Nozdormu, the Timeless One, blessed it. When Teldrassil was raised, Nozdormu judged the night elves' desire as arrogant and refused to bestow his blessing upon the new tree.

Travelers must head through Darnassus to the pink portal in the Temple Gardens, which transports them down to Rut'theran Village at the trunk's base. From Rut'theran, a ship sails across the sea to Auberdine on the mainland of Darkshore, alongside available hippogryph routes.

The entire zone is situated atop the living branches and wood of a colossal World Tree rather than natural continental rock. Because there are no stony subterranean crusts, no metal veins or ore deposits form here, though herbs flourish in great abundance.

A sinister presence has begun to seep into Teldrassil's unblessed roots. Sickness has corrupted the local water and flora, driving peaceful timberlings and the Gnarlpine furbolg tribe into frenzied aggression, while remnants of satyrs actively cultivate the taint.

Shadowglen is a sheltered, secluded vale on the eastern boughs of Teldrassil surrounding the great tree Aldrassil. It serves as a peaceful sanctuary where young night elves begin their training before venturing into the wider world.

Thunder Bluff. Thunder Bluff is the magnificent capital city of the tauren, perched atop windswept red-rock mesas rising above the grasslands of Mulgore. Founded by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof after uniting the nomadic tribes with the aid of the New Horde, it serves as the cultural, spiritual, and mercantile heart of his people. Connected by swaying rope bridges and wooden lifts, the city offers safety from centaur marauders and a peaceful sanctuary for travelers across Kalimdor. For countless generations, the tauren lived as nomadic wanderers across Kalimdor, locked in a brutal struggle for survival against ravenous centaur tribes. That desperate era ended during the Third War when Cairne Bloodhoof joined forces with Warchief Thrall. Together, the orcs and tauren broke the centaur assaults and secured the lush pastures of Mulgore. To protect their future, Cairne led the allied tribes to the safety of these natural stone bastions, founding Thunder Bluff as the first unified, permanent home the tauren had possessed in centuries.

High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof rules Thunder Bluff and leads the united tauren tribes. Revered for his wisdom, patience, and mighty strength, Cairne founded the city after allying with Thrall's Horde and driving the centaur from Mulgore.

Visitors arriving on foot or kodo must ride massive wooden platform elevators located on the southwestern and northeastern sides of the central mesa. Alternatively, the city features a Wind Rider roost with flight paths across Kalimdor.

Centuries of nomadic existence were marked by relentless hit-and-run attacks from aggressive centaur clans. The sheer cliffs of Mulgore's bluffs provide natural defense, shielding the tauren's dwellings, smiths, and sacred elders from ground ambushes and allowing them to permanently settle in peace.

The city spans a central mesa (divided into lower, middle, and high tiers) surrounded by three outer mesas. Hunter Rise is dedicated to warriors, hunters, and tracking lodges. Elder Rise is home to druids, wisemen, and the Grimtotem faction. Spirit Rise holds shrines to the Earth Mother, trainers of shamans, priests, and mages, and the cavernous Pools of Vision.

The Pools of Vision are sacred underground caverns tucked beneath Spirit Rise. Tauren seers, spiritwalkers, and practitioners of the arcane gather in these quiet, mist-shrouded waters to commune with the elements and interpret omens regarding the future of their people.

Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch and Elder Crone of the formidable Grimtotem clan. While she resides on Elder Rise and outwardly participates in Cairne's council, she is fiercely traditional, distrusting outsiders and quietly challenging the Bloodhoof tribe's soft stance toward the Horde.

Tirisfal Glades. Tirisfal Glades is the haunting northern territory of Lordaeron, now serving as the heartland of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken. Beneath blighted skies and rotting boughs lie fallen manors, dormant crypts, and the vast underground capital of the Undercity. Surrounded by mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders, it is a perilous realm where free-willed undead carve out their survival. Once the fertile cradle of humanity, Tirisfal Glades has withered beneath the curse of the Lich King's plague. The sun rarely penetrates the murky gloom, casting an eternal sickly pale over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches, and cold coastal hills. While remnants of old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead remain, their former masters have largely been swept into mass graves or risen as restless dead. Despite the devastation, a dark resilience permeates the countryside, anchored by towns like Brill and the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life.

During the Third War, Prince Arthas and the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the Kingdom of Lordaeron. The magical blight poisoned not only the populace, but the soil, trees, and water itself, leaving the glades in an eternal state of eerie, sickly decay.

The Forsaken are undead who broke free from the Lich King's telepathic domination after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, choosing to follow Lady Sylvanas Windrunner with their own free will. The Scourge roaming the farmsteads and ruins remain mindless slaves bound to the Lich King's commands.

They belong to the Scarlet Crusade, an uncompromising splinter order of former Silver Hand paladins and survivors. Convinced all undead are irredeemable abominations that must be purified by sword and fire, they execute both mindless thralls and free-willed Forsaken with fanatical hatred.

The region is named in honor of the titan keeper Tyr. According to legend, Tyr fell in battle against eldritch horrors in this glade. In the ancient vrykul tongue, 'Tyr's Fall' evolved into the name 'Tirisfal,' and the keeper's silver hand became an emblem woven deeply into early human mythology.

Newly awakened Forsaken emerge from the crypts of the Shadow Grave inside Deathknell, a cloistered town nestled in southwestern Tirisfal. There, administrators and executors evaluate whether the risen dead possess the sanity and loyalty required to serve the Dark Lady.

A large goblin-operated zeppelin tower sits on the hillside south of Brill, right outside the Ruins of Lordaeron. These airships provide direct, regular transit across the seas to Orgrimmar in Kalimdor and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

Undercity. Deep beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City lies the Undercity, the dark stronghold of the Forsaken. Originally carved out of ancient royal crypts and dungeons by the Scourge, it was seized by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and remade into an impenetrable subterranean sanctuary. Today it serves as the seat of Forsaken power and the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms. Long before the plague swept Lordaeron, the catacombs, dungeons, and sewers beneath the palace were collectively known as the Undercity. It held the tombs of nobility, the kingdom's deepest prisons—where the former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was once held before his escape—and the poorest denizens of the realm. When Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas and laid waste to the capital in 20 ADP, the prince ordered his undead servants to excavate and expand the subterranean passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule.

Beneath the palace of Lordaeron lay the ancient crypts of human royalty, along with the city's dungeon complex and vast sewer network. It housed prisoners of war, including Orgrim Doomhammer, as well as destitute citizens living in the subterranean shadows. After sacking the capital, Prince Arthas began turning these catacombs into a Scourge fortress before Sylvanas captured them.

The surface city of Lordaeron was utterly ruined during the Third War, making it difficult to defend against the Scarlet Crusade, Scourge forces, and Alliance survivors. The subterranean tunnels offered natural fortification, choke points, and secrecy, allowing the Forsaken to complete the Scourge's initial construction and thrive unseen.

The city is ruled by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen and Queen of the Forsaken. She governs from the Royal Quarter, guarded by Forsaken royal sentries and her subjugated dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras.

Above the city's main lifts sits a stone memorial for the slain King Terenas Menethil II. It does not contain his body, as his corpse was cremated and his ashes discarded during Kel'Thuzad's resurrection. Surviving Alliance humans bravely carved the monument amidst the ruins so the memory of Lordaeron's last true king would endure.

In the ruined throne room above the Undercity lifts, spectral echoes of the past still linger. Visitors standing in the center can hear faint phantom sounds: the celebratory bells and rose petals of Arthas's return, the warning words of the prophet Medivh, and the final conversation between King Terenas and his patricidal son.

The Forsaken formed an alliance of convenience with Warchief Thrall's Horde for survival, surrounded as they are by hostile Scarlet zealots and Scourge legions. While living Horde races find the toxic fumes and alchemical rivers stifling, emissaries and travelers are allowed access to foster diplomatic and military ties.

Wailing Caverns. Tucked beneath the Lushwater Oasis in the arid Barrens lies the Wailing Caverns, a labyrinthine system of subterranean springs and fissures named for the eerie whistling of trapped steam. What began as a noble druidic effort to revitalize Kalimdor's sun-bleached savanna has devolved into a warped, poisonous underworld. The caverns now teem with twisted wildlife and fallen disciples corrupted by a deep, unnatural nightmare. The night elf druid Naralex originally discovered this vast water system and devised an ambitious design: by opening a conduit straight into the Emerald Dream, he would siphon pure primal life essence through the subterranean springs, transforming the parched Barrens back into a thriving, verdant paradise. Deep in the Cavern of Mists, Naralex slipped into communion with the Dream, anchored by his loyal acolytes. Tragically, rather than tapping into pure vitality, the druid's sleeping mind touched the Emerald Nightmare. The festering corruption instantly seized him, transforming his well-intentioned conduit into a valve pouring venom and madness into the underground waterways.

Westfall. Once the fertile breadbasket of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Westfall has collapsed into a windswept, neglected territory overrun by outlaws. Deprived of official crown support and military garrisons, its surviving homesteaders cling to their farms while the Defias Brotherhood tightens its grip from the abandoned mining town of Moonbrook. For generations, Westfall fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Its rolling pastures and wheat fields flourished until the aftermath of the Second War brought financial exhaustion and political neglect. When the kingdom poured its resources elsewhere and failed to maintain its garrisons, the territory grew fallow. Today, barren pastures, howling coastal gusts, rogue harvest golems, and raiding Riverpaw gnolls make daily survival a constant trial for the stubborn few who refuse to abandon their homesteads.

Wetlands. The Wetlands is a vast, mist-shrouded swamp nestled between the mountains of Khaz Modan and the shores of Baradin Bay. Historically battered by dwarven wars and orcish invasions, it serves as a rugged buffer zone between Ironforge and the northern lands of Lordaeron. The fortified port of Menethil Harbor stands as the Alliance's primary lifeline in a sodden wilderness overrun by Dragonmaw orcs, murlocs, and gnolls. Spreading out beneath the towering precipice of the Stonewrought Dam, the Wetlands is a cold, waterlogged expanse cloaked in perpetual fog and uniform gray skies. While once home to thriving dwarven settlements, the marshlands are now scattered with sunken stone ruins, sodden bogs, and treacherous mires. Adventurers entering the region must navigate narrow passes, either coming north through the barricaded defile of Dun Algaz from Loch Modan or crossing the towering arches of the Thandol Span from the Arathi Highlands.

Zephras Isle. Zephras Isle is a flying island suspended within Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air. It serves as the ancestral starting home of the Skyborne, whose society now faces an existential crisis as the island's sustaining magic steadily erodes. With contact severed from neighboring sky-realms, its inhabitants struggle against elemental collapse and arriving refugees. Zephras Isle is an isolated landmass adrift in the endless winds of Skywall. For generations, the Skyborne lived here alongside native air elementals who helped preserve the magical currents holding the isle aloft. However, several centuries ago, those elemental stewards vanished entirely. Deprived of their presence and guardianship, the latent enchantments upholding the land have slowly begun to fail, causing Zephras to slowly fracture and destabilize.
Zephras Isle is situated inside Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air, rather than upon the surface of Azeroth. It floats among the perpetual clouds and wind currents of this ethereal domain.

The island relied on the presence of native air elementals who once coexisted with the Skyborne. Several centuries ago, these elementals vanished, leaving the magical foundations that anchor and preserve the flying land to slowly weaken and decay over time.

They are neighboring floating islands in Skywall also populated by the Skyborne. Zephras Isle lost communication with both when the elementals disappeared, and fleeing refugees now report that both Anvilas and Siroccas are collapsing into oblivion.

The Skyborne operate skydocks at the settlement of Valanaar. Airships launch from these docks across the planar boundary to Azeroth, landing near Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains and at Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.

The Skyborne are the inhabitants who make their home on Zephras Isle and its sister sky-realms. Having dwelled in Skywall for generations, they now face the slow destruction of their flying homeland as its binding magic fades.
Aside from peaceful villages and visiting refugees, the island is troubled by local bandits, cavern-dwelling nightclaws, and beasts inhabiting areas like the Shriekling Den and Nightclaw Cavern.
